key_insight: Autocata turns catalyst screening into a language-driven, capability-centric workflow that automatically maps reaction-network goals to specialized generative models and evaluation pipelines.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce expert bottlenecks in computational catalyst design by automating multi-step setup, candidate generation, validity checks, and ranking across complex reaction pathways.
method: Pretrained a Transformer on 2 million catalyst–adsorbate structures to learn chemistry-aware representations.
Built a registry of 79 adsorbate-specialized generative models covering carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and hydrogen intermediates.
Uses an autonomous agent to parse natural-language goals, select capabilities, generate candidates, filter invalid structures, and run ML-potential evaluations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on CH4 activation, nitrogen reduction, and CO2-to-methanol pathways, showing the system can execute and reconfigure screening workflows across multiple reaction networks.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the coverage and accuracy of the capability registry, so tasks outside the embedded reaction-network models could still require human intervention.
paper_title: Autocata: Reaction-network-guided autonomous catalyst screening via capability-centric AI
